A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FLARE. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support matching retained, revised, and removed content.

before.justification: v1 reports original pose-estimation, reconstruction, rendering, ablation, and input-view sensitivity results in Tables 1–7 and accompanying figures.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical evaluations, including the appendix experiments, and revises several pose-estimation results.

M1.justification: Section 4.3 specifies an intrinsic-conditioned RealEstate10K variant and replaces v1's claim that camera parameters are unnecessary with freedom from camera extrinsics. This is a limited revision to the reported model inputs. The cascaded pose, geometry, and Gaussian architecture and losses remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The eight training datasets and the RealEstate10K, DL3DV, DTU, ETH3D, TUM, and BlendedMVS evaluation coverage are retained. The appendix's dense reconstruction and varying-view scenarios already appear in v1.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding Tables 1–7. PoseDiffusion remains evaluated despite removal of its training-dataset note; its changed scores do not constitute a baseline replacement.

E3.justification: The reported RealEstate10K rendering configuration explicitly includes intrinsic conditioning in v4, qualifying v1's camera-parameter-free description. Two-view inputs, the low/medium-overlap split, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish reruns or a changed PoseDiffusion training regime.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Table 5, MVSplat input-view analysis in Figure 5, FLARE view-count study in Table 6, and qualitative examples are retained. The new explanation of variable-length inputs adds no experimental analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable experimental uncertainty estimates. The method's predicted confidence maps are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 substantially revises the pose comparison: PoseDiffusion's RRA/RTA/AUC changes from 0.91/0.73/78.2 to 0.78/0.27/51.6, while FLARE changes from 0.97/0.74/84.6 to 0.97/0.65/79.9. PoseDiffusion falls below VGGSfM, MASt3R, and DUSt3R in AUC; FLARE remains first. These unexplained revisions materially change the comparative margins. Tables 2–7 retain their results.

T1.justification: Equations 1–12 and their mathematical content are retained; neither version adds theoretical propositions or proofs. Correcting the prose reference from Cf to Pf aligns it with the already unchanged Equation 4.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: efficient feed-forward reconstruction, camera-guided cascaded learning, two-stage geometry estimation, and state-of-the-art performance. The shortened conclusion does not remove claims retained elsewhere.

C2.justification: v4 removes the specific limitations concerning thin structures and out-of-distribution camera trajectories. It clarifies intrinsic versus extrinsic requirements and memory-limited input counts, and attributes pose performance to joint geometry learning rather than geometry and appearance. Other experimental interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v4 removes Appendix C and Tables 8–10, including the CroCo encoder identification, detailed component architectures, and appearance-head specification. It also removes staged training/freezing instructions, batch sizes, and default loss weights. Reference/source token duplication is newly explained, while preprocessing, the main training budget, and the project/code link remain.

R1.justification: The CroCo v2 reference disappears with the architecture appendix. The other cited works and substantive related-work positioning remain unchanged after matching renumbered references.

P1.justification: v4 standardizes 'point maps,' refines token terminology, shortens the discussion, adds an Appendix heading, and expands the acknowledgements with funding information. It removes the limitations and architecture subsections, but most prose and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Architecture Tables 8–10 disappear, retained result tables move within the main text, and appendix Table 7 becomes smaller. Figure 1's caption is edited and Figure 2 is re-rendered, while the figures retain their substantive content and the overall two-column design remains.

improvement.justification: v4 clarifies intrinsic conditioning and variable-view handling, but removes useful architecture specifications, training settings, and concrete failure disclosures. Deleting the conflicting appendix training-budget account improves consistency without supplying a complete replacement recipe. With the core evidence largely retained and the score revisions unexplained, the clearest net effect is reduced reproducibility and transparency.
